# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ☝ 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✌ ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤟 ☝]

I need to figure out what these gestures mean. Mute is trying to communicate something using gestures since Mute can't speak to me directly in a way I'd understand without context - wait, actually Mute CAN speak, and I can hear speech too. But here Mute chose to gesture, meaning this is likely information from the manual that Mute wants to convey to me (visual) rather than to Blind (who can't see gestures).

Let me think about what I see: DISPLAY [0], LIGHT [blue], BUTTON [large], WIRES 1:blue 2:green 3:yellow.

The gestures use 👍 ☝ 🤟, 👍 ✌ ✌, 👍 🤟 ☝ - three sequences of 3 symbols each. This could be mapping to my three wires, or could be numbered instructions. Since I can't hear Mute's speech to Blind, I'm missing context. I should report what I see to Mute (who can read manual and match against my observations) since Mute can hear me.

I'll describe the bomb clearly to Mute so they can cross-reference with the manual, and acknowledge I received gestures but don't yet know their meaning - I need more context or a key.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I see: display shows 0, light is blue, a large button labeled push to defeat, and three wires - wire 1 blue, wire 2 green, wire 3 yellow. I received your three gesture groups but do not know what they mean yet - please continue speaking to guide me, since I cannot hear what you tell Blind.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤟 ☝]

Mute is repeating a gesture sequence to me: 👍 🤟 ☝. This matches the third sequence from before (👍 🤟 ☝). Since Mute can't speak (mute can't speak at all - only gesture and I misunderstood earlier, Mute literally cannot speak, only gesture or the manual reading is silent). Wait - rules say Mute cannot speak. So my request for Mute to "speak" was impossible. Mute can only gesture to me, and gesture to Blind isn't possible since Blind can't see gestures either. So Mute's only channel to convey manual info to me is gestures, and to Blind... Mute has no direct channel to Blind at all! Mute must relay through me or Blind speaks to relay through... wait Blind can speak too (only Deaf can't hear/touch... let me recheck: Blind cannot see or touch printed things but CAN speak/hear presumably).

Actually only Deaf cannot hear. Blind can hear and speak. So Mute must gesture to me (Deaf), and I must relay via speech to Blind, since I hear nothing but I can speak and Blind can hear.

Given that, Mute is trying to send me a message via gestures, repeating group 3: 👍 🤟 ☝. This likely refers to wire 3 (yellow) - perhaps telling me which wire to check or confirming something about wire 3. I should acknowledge receipt and try to establish a code, or relay to Blind that a message is coming.

I'll try establishing shared reference: my wires are numbered 1,2,3. Mute repeating the 3rd sequence twice suggests it's important - maybe it's the wire to cut. I'll relay a guess to Blind and ask Mute (via my own speech, which Mute can't hear) - but Mute can't hear me either! Mute can only read gestures/writing? No - Mute cannot speak, but nothing says Mute can't hear. Let me recheck table: Mute "Cannot: Speak, or touch bomb." So Mute CAN hear. Good, so I can speak to Mute.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I see wire 3 is yellow. If your gesture group repeated three times means wire 3, blink twice by repeating it again. Otherwise gesture once for wire 1, twice for wire 2, three times for wire 3 to tell me which wire matters.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝]

Mute repeated ☝ three times - this seems to be an acknowledgment or confirmation matching my own single ☝ gesture, but tripled. Let me reconsider: maybe Mute is using gesture sequences as a simple code where each gesture corresponds to a specific letter/number/instruction from the manual, not something I should guess blindly.

Since Mute can hear my speech, and I can hear nothing from anyone, all information from Blind must also route through Mute repeating it as gestures to me, or I just don't get Blind's info directly at all. Let me stop guessing at codes and instead ask Mute direct yes/no questions I can answer by gesturing back, since gesture is our only shared reliable channel (Mute sees my gestures? Wait - Mute cannot see! Only Deaf can see. So Mute does NOT receive my gestures at all - gestures only go to those who can see, which is only me (Deaf) among the three of us... wait, can Blind see? No, Blind cannot see. So I am the ONLY one who can see gestures!

That means my gestures to Mute are useless - Mute cannot see them. I made an error. Only speech reaches Mute (Mute can hear). So I should only speak to Mute, never gesture.

And Mute's gestures only reach me. So Mute uses gestures to send me manual info, and I must relay via speech to both Mute and Blind.

Let me try a cleaner protocol: ask Mute to gesture wire number using count of a single symbol, avoiding my mistaken gesture reply.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Sorry, you cannot see my gestures, only I can see yours - I will only speak from now. Please gesture just a number of taps with one symbol: one tap for wire 1, two taps for wire 2, three taps for wire 3, to tell me which wire is safe to cut.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝]

Mute repeated the same three-☝ gesture again, likely before receiving my latest message (turn ordering: Mute goes first each round, so Mute's turn 4 gesture was sent before seeing my turn 3 speech). This is just a delay artifact - my message from turn 3 will reach Mute now, and Mute's next gesture (turn 5) should respond to it.

I'll wait to see if Mute adjusts, but I should also proactively relay bomb details to Blind now, since Blind needs my visual info too (relayed through speech, which Blind can hear directly from me).

```
speak(to="blind", text="Here is what the bomb looks like: display reads 0, indicator light is blue, there is one large button labeled push to defuse, and three wires - wire 1 is blue, wire 2 is green, wire 3 is yellow. Wait for Mute's instructions on which wire or button to use.")
speak(to="mute", text="Still seeing the same triple tap gesture as last round - that was likely sent before my request reached you. Please now gesture once for wire 1, twice for wire 2, or three times for wire 3, whichever the manual says is safe.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝]

Mute keeps sending the exact same gesture: ☝ ☝ ☝ (three single-finger points), unchanged across three rounds. This is suspicious - either Mute is stuck repeating a pre-decided message that doesn't fit my counting scheme, or this triple-☝ itself IS the intended message, not a response to my counting request (maybe Mute hasn't adapted, or this is simply their fixed way of saying "wire 3" using a different convention, or it says something else entirely like "all three wires" or "none of them").

Given it hasn't changed despite my requests, let me consider: maybe ☝ repeated 3 times means "wire one" said three times for emphasis, not "wire 3" via counting. Or it could mean 1-1-1, referencing something else like a code "111". Let me try a completely different tack - ask targeted yes/no questions Mute can answer with distinct single gestures.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I will ask yes or no questions. Please answer by gesturing thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no. Question: does the manual say to cut wire number 1?")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

Mute answered 👎 (no) to "does the manual say to cut wire 1?" This is real progress - we have a working yes/no protocol now.

Let me continue narrowing down with yes/no questions.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Good, thumbs down received, understood as no. Next question: does the manual say to cut wire number 2, the green one?")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

Not wire 2 either. So by elimination it should be wire 3 (yellow) - which matches Mute's earlier repeated "☝ ☝ ☝" possibly meaning wire 3 all along, or something else entirely. Let me confirm with a direct question.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Understood, not wire 2. So is it wire number 3, the yellow one, that should be cut?")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Confirmed: wire 3 (yellow) should be cut. Now I need to relay this to Blind, who can hear my speech and act on the bomb.

But let me also verify there's nothing else needed - button should NOT be pushed presumably, and I should check if display/light matter. Let me relay the wire instruction to Blind now, and also double check with Mute if only cutting the wire is needed or if there's more to it (like order of operations, or whether button should never be pressed).

```
speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire number 3, the yellow wire. Do not touch the other wires or the button yet.")
speak(to="mute", text="Confirmed wire 3, yellow, relaying to Blind now. Is cutting that single wire the complete solution, or is there more to do - such as pressing the button after, or an order to follow? Please gesture thumbs up if cutting wire 3 alone defuses it, thumbs down if more steps remain.")
```
